name: Andrew Kreitz
current_role: Co-founder & CFO, Castelion (hypersonic strike weapons manufacturer, Torrance CA)
profile: Ex-SpaceX finance lead who co-founded Castelion in 2022 with fellow SpaceX alumni Bryon Hargis (CEO) and Sean Pitt (COO). As CFO he has led fundraising, including a $1B Series C that funds Project Ranger, a hypersonic-weapons manufacturing campus in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, where production of the Blackbeard strike system is due to begin in early 2027.
interesting_fact: Castelion builds its own solid rocket motors and flight computers and ran 21 flight tests in 2025 alone; its Blackbeard hypersonic system is under contract with both the U.S. Navy and Army.
deep_cut_fact: Before SpaceX (where he ran financial planning and government cost proposals for classified programs) he was a VP in Goldman Sachs' aerospace & defense investment-banking group, executing more than $10B of M&A; he holds a UCLA BA and a Chicago Booth MBA.
notes: He is CFO, not CEO (Bryon Hargis is CEO). Low public profile; route via Castelion media@ address or media-kit form. Defense/manufacturing angle fits energy/industrial podcast themes.

name: Colin Zima
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Omni Analytics (BI / semantic-layer platform)
profile: Data executive who spent ~8 years at Looker, rising to Chief Analytics Officer and VP of Product, and stayed on at Google after its $2.6B Looker acquisition. In 2022 he co-founded Omni with college friends Jamie Davidson and Chris Merrick; the AI-driven analytics platform is valued around $2B.
interesting_fact: Earlier he co-founded restaurant-pricing startup PrimaTable with Jamie Davidson, which was acquired by HotelTonight, where he went on to lead data teams before joining Looker.
deep_cut_fact: Omni's own bio notes he has been applying data since he wrote his college thesis on in-game NFL betting; he also worked on Google's Search quality team.

public_contacts.value: Guest on First Round Review 'In Depth' episode 108

notes: Accessible, frequent podcast guest. His work email is published on Omni's team page. Omni has a Santa Cruz hub; team posts weekly engineering demos on YouTube.

name: Chen Yuanpei
current_role: Co-founder (head of reinforcement learning), PsiBot / 灵初智能, Shanghai
profile: Post-2000s Chinese robotics researcher (陈源培, also written 陈元培) who studied under Peking University RL scholar Yang Yaodong and was a Stanford visiting scholar with Fei-Fei Li and Karen Liu. In 2024 he co-founded PsiBot, which builds dexterous robot hands and RL-based embodied-AI models trained on human data; it raised a 2B-yuan round and is valued ~$1B.
interesting_fact: PsiBot's robot played 30 minutes of continuous mahjong against visitors at WAIC 2025 in Shanghai; Chen was named to Forbes Asia 30 Under 30 in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He began researching dexterous robot hands in his first and second years of university simply because he found them fascinating ('dexterous hands are really cool'), and attended WAIC as a spectator for years before exhibiting there as a founder in 2025.
notes: CEO is Wang Qibin; Chen is the technical co-founder. He is lead author of the Bi-DexHands RL benchmark (PKU), likely the same person given the PKU/Yang Yaodong link, but not explicitly confirmed. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Jesse Moore
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, M-KOPA (connected-asset fintech for African 'everyday earners', HQ London/Nairobi)
profile: Canadian-born entrepreneur who moved to Nairobi in 2010 and co-founded M-KOPA with Nick Hughes and Chad Larson, initially selling pay-as-you-go solar home systems via M-PESA. M-KOPA has since pivoted to smartphone, loan and e-mobility financing and reports 10 million customers and ~$600M revenue.
interesting_fact: M-KOPA grew out of pay-as-you-go solar: customers paid for off-grid solar kits in small daily mobile-money installments, a model that later extended to smartphones and digital loans.
deep_cut_fact: At UNC (Morehead Scholar '01) he majored in communication studies, a major only six other students shared; his first job was at Monitor Group, then five years with CARE. He says he arrived in Kenya with 'four PowerPoint slides, no money, no name, and no products.'
notes: Strong energy-access angle (off-grid solar). Oxford Said MBA (Skoll Scholar), ex-Vodafone. Frequent conference speaker (MWC, Africa CEO Forum).
